candidates.tagline: Politician paints a DIY 'No Cycling' ban on the pavement. It says the opposite.
candidates.story: DUP councillor Kyle Moutray spray-painted an unofficial 'No Cycling' stencil on a Portadown pavement on August 26, 2026, but added an extra slash that creates a double negative — effectively 'no prohibited cycling' — and chose blue/yellow Irish road sign colors, accidentally using the iconography of the Republic he opposes.
candidates.why_funny: The sign he painted to ban cycling technically legalises it, and the pro-British Unionist politician did it in the exact colours used on Irish road signs.
candidates.alt: DUP councillor Kyle Moutray crouching on a Portadown footpath, spray-painting a blue-and-yellow stencil of a bicycle with a double-slash — a double-negative 'No Cycling' sign

candidates.tagline: 9 months, 7 yellow stripes, over a crater field. She called it 'infrastructure'.
candidates.story: LA Councilwoman and mayoral candidate Nithya Raman celebrated a 'completed' crosswalk on August 26, 2026 — eight months after residents first asked for it — posting a photo of fresh yellow paint applied directly over a severely cracked, pothole-riddled street.
candidates.why_funny: The photo intended to show an infrastructure win instead shows yellow stripes stretched across what looks like a road-shaped jigsaw puzzle, with every crack still gaping underneath.
candidates.alt: Freshly painted yellow crosswalk stripes over a badly cracked and crumbling Los Angeles street, with deep fissures visible between and beneath the new paint
